::: {#thm-run-last}
#### A run ends where the extended transition function says

Let $M = (S, \Sigma, \delta, s_0)$ be a state machine (@def-state-machine), let $s \in S$,
and let $r_0, \ldots, r_n$ be the run (@def-run) of $M$ on a string $w = x_1 \cdots x_n$ from $s$.
Then

$$
r_n = \delta^*(s, w),
$$

where $\delta^*$ is the extended transition function (@def-extended-transition).

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

We show, by induction (@def-proof-by-induction) on $k = 0, 1, \ldots, n$,
that $r_k = \delta^*(s, x_1 \cdots x_k)$, where $x_1 \cdots x_0$ is the empty string $\lambda$.

**Base case.**
For $k = 0$, $r_0 = s = \delta^*(s, \lambda)$, by @def-run and the base case of @def-extended-transition.

**Inductive step.**
Suppose $r_{k - 1} = \delta^*(s, x_1 \cdots x_{k - 1})$ for some $k$ with $1 \le k \le n$.
Then

$$
\ba
r_k
&= \delta(r_{k - 1}, x_k)
&& \text{(definition of the run)}
\\&= \delta\paren{\delta^*(s, x_1 \cdots x_{k - 1}), x_k}
&& \text{(induction hypothesis)}
\\&= \delta^*(s, x_1 \cdots x_{k - 1} x_k).
&& \text{(recursive rule for } \delta^* \text{)}
\ea
$$

By induction, the equation holds for every $k \le n$, and $k = n$ gives $r_n = \delta^*(s, w)$.

:::

:::
